summary.text: Laura Jones is the Democratic nominee for the open U.S. House seat in Texas's 8th District. A Houston native, she has worked as a business professional and real estate sales agent and describes herself as a small business owner and Army mom. She has sought the seat in each cycle since 2020 and is running on affordability, a higher minimum wage and Medicare for All.

paragraphs.text: Laura Jones was born and raised in Houston, Texas. In a 2020 Ballotpedia survey she described herself as a native Texan, wife, mother and business professional who had raised six children with her husband and operated a business.
Ballotpedia lists her career experience as a business professional and a real estate sales agent with HomePlus Realty Group.

She said in 2020 that she had served for a year as chair of the San Jacinto County Democrats and as field director for Texas Senate District 3 under the Texas Democratic Party's Non-Urban Rural Caucus, and that she and her husband had moved to a rural East Texas town.
Her campaign website describes her as a lifelong Texan, Army mom, small business owner and working-class American.
Jones first ran for Texas's 8th Congressional District in 2020, when she lost the Democratic primary to Elizabeth Hernandez.

She won the Democratic nomination in 2022 and lost the general election to Republican Morgan Luttrell, 68.1% to 30.5%, then won the nomination again in 2024 and lost to Luttrell, by then the incumbent, 68.2% to 31.8%.
After Texas redrew the district and Luttrell chose not to seek re-election, she won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary over Keith Coleman, 65.7% to 34.3%.
